policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the name as 'Izhar'; its mapped textual-variant note identifies 'Zohar' as another reading, distinguishing the ketiv r01 as the reading represented in the main text.
ASV renders the name as 'Tilon', which distinguishes the qere/base reading r00-base from the ketiv alternative.
ASV renders the people as 'the Meunim', which distinguishes the qere/base reading r00-base; the Hebrew-gloss note concerns 'destroyed them utterly' and does not map to this name.
